title: Shop Ready, global chat and calmer bots
changes: The shop has a Ready button: once every player is ready, the shop ends 3 seconds later (never before 6 seconds).
Knocked out for the round? Your round gold arrives right away, and the knockout card opens the shop.
Global chat in the main menu: everyone can read it, and signed-in players with a name can post.
Bots move more like players: far less turning back and forth on the spot, and they no longer all react on the same beat.
King of the Hill: taking the hill takes half a second, quick play goes to 75 tickets, and a force field seals the hill for the first 5 seconds of every fight.
Your email no longer shows in the main menu; Account settings keeps it hidden until you ask.
Ranked: the announcer calls Match Point and Final Round at the right moments.

title: Friendlier casual games and a quicker hill
changes: Casual games now fill with a mix of Medium and Hard bots instead of mostly Hard.
King of the Hill: taking the hill takes 1 second instead of 1.75.
The wardrobe now needs an account: sign in to earn Embers, unlock pieces and wear them in games.
Brawlock is also on itch.io. Players there play as guests and can sign in here for ranked, Embers and the wardrobe.

title: Fresh start, hill pillars and sharper dodging
changes: King of the Hill: taking the hill takes 1.75 seconds, and an enemy brushing it pauses your capture instead of restarting it.
King of the Hill: pillars ring the hill, on its corners or its tips depending on the round, plus a few random ones.
Outside ranked, Fresh start sells your whole build for 75% of what you paid on it, before the next fight.
The scoreboard shows each player's net worth, and results rows open to show their final build.
While you are down, click a name in the top bar to watch that player.
Hard, Brutal and Uber bots read wind-ups and dodge close Fireballs; their lobby ratings were remeasured.
The centre tile no longer glows outside King of the Hill.

title: Hill tuning and sharper bots
changes: Taking the hill takes 3 seconds before the first ticket; contesting it starts that over.
The hill keeps shrinking with a small arena, down to the centre tile.
Hill gold is tuned down: 1, 1, 2, 2, then 3 every 5 seconds.
Reaching the ticket target ends the match at once, at exactly the target.
Bots go after whoever holds the hill, chase a runaway leader and hold grudges.
Bots no longer throw away Scourge blasts that would hit, knock Scourge casters away when they can, and buy masteries.
Leaving a casual game keeps it rejoinable from the menu for 2 minutes.
Casual lobbies wait 60 seconds once a second player joins; Ready still starts sooner.

title: Gold on the hill
changes: Standing on the hill pays gold every 5 seconds, even while it is contested: 1 gold, then one more each time you stay, up to 5. Stepping off starts over.
A ring beside each warlock's name shows how close their next hill gold is and how much it pays.

title: A calmer, tighter hill
changes: King of the Hill starts with a smaller hill, so holding it alone for a ticket is possible again.
A contested hill shows a calm outline instead of flashing.

title: King of the Hill
changes: King of the Hill: hold the glowing hill with no enemy on it to earn a ticket every second. First to 100 tickets wins. Play it from the main menu as a casual free-for-all.
The hill shrinks by one ring every 90 seconds and blinks red before it does. A plate under the clock shows who holds it and the ticket race to the target.
Custom games can play King of the Hill in rounds or with respawns, and bots fight for the hill.
Game servers run 30 updates a second instead of 60, so each server can host several times more games. Your own moves still show at once.
Every bot build buys Boots early and levels them.
Projectiles fly exactly their listed range, and Homing missiles sound calmer in flight.
Denied calls only play when you escape close to death.
Match history shows Elo in whole points and player names in their colours.

title: Clearer combat at a glance
changes: A slim strip above your abilities shows health, healing per second and accumulated knockback.
Toggle FPS with F2 beside your connection indicator. Click the readout for diagnostics that distinguish local stalls from round-trip delay.
In-game chat stays transparent when idle and uses a light backing while you type.
Collapsed betting stays at the right edge and shows whether you placed a bet. Reopen it to follow live odds.
Leave lobby stays at the top right. Bugs & feedback has a consistent place in menu footers.
Panel outlines follow their angled corners, including dialogs and ability cards.
Round-win announcements are shorter and more varied. Denied calls are reserved for close escapes and have a cooldown.

title: Find a game
changes: The main menu lists open games with real players under your player card. Join with one click, or see all games.
Browse games shows how many games are open and how many people are in them.
Taking over a bot seat between rounds hands you control as soon as the fight ends. If you take over a bot seat, Fresh start refunds its build so you can shop your own.
Custom games keep empty seats open between rounds, and rematches start only when everyone is ready.
The results screen fits one window, shows each player's ping and sits beside the room chat.
Guests keep their plain name, marked by a small icon in the lobby and results.
The account dialog shows your warlock, emblem and name. The wardrobe camera frames close and back views better.
The main menu fits the window without scrolling, with version, What's new and policies in the top-left corner. Maintenance notices only appear when they affect your region.

title: More time to gather
changes: Casual lobbies wait 30 seconds. Choose Wait for players to keep the room open; anyone ready can resume the countdown.
Everyone ready shortens casual and ranked countdowns to 10 seconds, with a clear start warning and sound.
Custom room settings carry over to your next room. Joins, leaves and disconnects appear in room chat.
Spectator winners split the betting pool. Each pick shows its potential payout.
Unfinished matches contribute to combat statistics. Leaving a counted game records a loss when it resolves.
Bots avoid shots that would hit an active Shield; Brutal and Uber punish more openings.
Tiles char as they sink, lava deaths fall more smoothly, and announcer warnings are better timed.
Bugs & feedback is easier to find, with arena screenshots and useful diagnostics. Privacy pages link directly to the feedback form.

title: Clicks reach the arena again
changes: Fixed: in alpha.6 mouse clicks in a match never reached the arena, so right-click opened the browser menu instead of moving.

title: Stay in the game
changes: New Wardrobe: try horns, hats, wings, cape emblems and staffs on a live 3D warlock, then unlock them with Embers. Looks only, never gameplay.
Browse menus and stats without leaving your lobby. Return in one click; hear when ranked finds players.
The menu now hosts ongoing battles between strong bots.
Your account shares one compact menu card. Lobby chat sits below settings, leaving room for the full player roster.
Spectator bets are easier to find, with visible picks and clear open, locked and closed states.
Leaving after 60 seconds of combat counts as a loss when the match ends, including ranked Elo. Rejoin before the end to recover.
Filter online match history by Casual or Ranked and inspect saved builds. What's new shows each update and earlier releases.
Send bugs or feedback from any menu, with a screenshot and useful game context attached automatically.

title: Sharper opponents
changes: Casual games mix Hard bots with one Brutal and one Medium opponent.
Bots punish warlocks who stand still.
Unattended results close after 30 minutes when nobody is ready.
Spell glows render more efficiently.

title: Fairer ranked results
changes: Ranked Elo follows the overall match result, fixing cases where the winner lost rating because of round survival order.

title: Ready when you are
changes: The next match waits until every human player presses Ready.
New game lets you find another room without waiting for a rematch.
When everyone is ready, the lobby countdown drops to five seconds.

title: Louder hits, clearer results
changes: Fireball and Scourge lead the hotbar, with voiced deaths and clearer kill callouts.
Casual matches play to three round wins.
Match history shows the full standings and earned Embers.
Betting closes earlier as the fight narrows.

title: The first public playtest
changes: Casual and ranked multiplayer across US and European servers.
Accounts, a cosmetic collection and guided practice.
Recover your room after a reload or disconnect.
